stories.headline: Thanksgiving online sales hit a record $7.1 billion as AI-referred visits rose 162%, Adobe says
stories.dek: The first holiday actuals show AI assistants sending more shoppers than Adobe forecast, and those visits buying more often.

facts.text: US online spending on Thanksgiving Day, up 10.4% from a year earlier and above Adobe's $6.9B forecast
the rise in AI-referred visits to US retail sites on Thanksgiving, against the 159% Adobe had projected
how much better AI-referred visits converted into purchases than other traffic, per Adobe's data as reported
Black Friday online spending through the afternoon, up 12.8%. Adobe now expects $13.0B to $13.4B for the day

open.label: Visits, not agent purchases
open.text: Adobe counts visits referred by AI tools, not purchases agents complete. The Black Friday total is not final, and these figures come via press write-ups of Adobe's data rather than an Adobe release we could read.

chart.title: US online spending, Cyber Week 2026, $ billions
chart.note: Adobe Analytics. Hatched bars are Adobe forecasts; Black Friday drawn at the low end of its range.

stories.headline: Banned Nvidia Blackwell racks turn up at a Shanghai site tied to Megaspeed, Bloomberg says
stories.dek: Chinese loan filings list a GB300 rack as collateral, the clearest sign yet that top US chips are reaching China despite the ban.

facts.text: about $14M, the loan Shanghai Shuoyao took from Shanghai Innovation Bank with a GB300 NVL72 rack as collateral
Blackwell Ultra chips in a GB300 NVL72 rack, alongside 36 Grace processors
a loan to Shanghai Kezhan, which disclosed a GB200 server at the same Yangtze River Delta Project site
the Taiwan maker Bloomberg traced the rack to through a public warranty database. It declined to name the buyer

open.label: How it got there
open.text: Bloomberg found no evidence that Megaspeed itself diverted the hardware. Shuoyao calls its Megaspeed work ordinary cooperation, Megaspeed denies wrongdoing, and Nvidia has not commented in these reports.

chart.title: Shanghai loans backed by or tied to Nvidia hardware, million yuan
chart.note: Per Bloomberg, as reported by Investing.com. Longjie shares Shuoyao's parent.

stories.headline: Nvidia halts AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries, the FT reports
stories.dek: Dell and Supermicro told buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia their orders will not ship as new US chip rules bite.

facts.text: countries, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, where Nvidia told partners including Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping servers with its chips
revenue Nvidia booked through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025, up 72%, per company accounts cited by the FT. Some of it is Taiwan and China revenue
in loans banks halted to Singapore cloud provider Aolani, which planned to rent computing to ByteDance, the FT reported
what cloud providers have to apply for a license under the new US rules. A cloud executive called it chaos

open.label: Anonymous and maybe temporary
open.text: The report rests on three people familiar with the matter. Nvidia, Dell and Supermicro did not respond to Reuters, and no source says how long the halt lasts. Bloomberg put Aolani's loan at $480M.

chart.title: Nvidia revenue booked in Singapore, $ billions
chart.note: Per the FT, from company accounts. *Derived: $104B divided by 1.72.

stories.headline: Lenders stall a $6.6 billion loan and other Asian data center deals after US chip curbs
stories.dek: Banks are reviewing deals tied to Bytedance, Alibaba and Tencent, Bloomberg reports, an early sign of how far the new rules reach.

facts.text: the upsized loan Bain Capital's Bridge Data Centres is seeking. Some lenders are delaying it for more due diligence. Its Malaysian sites serve Bytedance
countries, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil, where buyers now need a US license for advanced American AI chips under a rule announced last week
loan to GMI Cloud for chips for a Thai data center Tencent would use. At least one fund has dropped out
lent to Asia Pacific data center companies since 2023, up from virtually zero, by Bloomberg's count

open.label: Anonymous sourcing
open.text: The loan details come from people familiar with the talks. The companies declined to comment or did not reply. Sites already leasing a lot of compute to Chinese firms get 90 days to obtain a separate license.

Amazon's yearly advertising business, which shopping agents can bypass by skipping sponsored listings
big retailers already letting Muse search and buy: Walmart, Best Buy, Gap and Sephora

stories.headline: Nvidia ends the week at $150.49, well below Monday's $165.05, before Huang's House interview
stories.dek: S&P has its rating on watch, and Friday's Shanghai report adds to the export questions lawmakers will raise on Dec 1.

facts.text: Nvidia's rise on Nov 23, to $165.05, after the board reinstated Huang, its largest one-day percentage gain in more than two decades
Friday's close, up 0.8% on the day and 8.8% below Monday's close (derived), after a 5.86% fall to $155.38 on Tuesday
Nvidia's issuer rating, which S&P put on CreditWatch Negative over board independence and succession. A one-notch cut could come within 90 days
Huang's closed-door interview before three House committees, including Intelligence. General counsel Tim Teter follows the next day

open.label: Unresolved
open.text: A committee of independent directors is still investigating reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, with no end date.

stories.headline: Anthropic jumps 10.98% to $91.88, back above its $83 IPO price
stories.dek: ANT rose with a broad AI rally in Friday's short session. Up to 303 million more shares can be sold from Dec 15.

facts.text: ANT's close on Nov 27, up $9.09, after two sessions below the $83 IPO price
Friday's trading range. Volume was about 143.6M shares, well under the 353.1M average
shares that can unlock on Dec 15, after about 315M were freed on the first trading day
when FTSE Russell will add Anthropic after the close, if it meets fast entry rules

open.label: No company news
open.text: None of the reports ties the jump to Anthropic news. They credit a broad return to risky assets: the Nasdaq rose 2.31% on Friday and 6.7% for the week. The 52-week high is $115.10.

stories.headline: Dell's AI server backlog reaches $132.3 billion after $60.2 billion of orders in one quarter
stories.dek: Revenue doubled to $54.9 billion and Dell raised its full-year target to $202 billion, a read on how much AI hardware is still on order.

facts.text: Dell's AI backlog at the end of the quarter, after it booked $60.2B of AI orders
AI server revenue in the quarter, up 291% from $5.6B a year earlier
total revenue, up 103%, against about $49.3B Wall Street expected. Shares rose nearly 4% after hours
full-year revenue guidance, raised from $192B, including $78B of AI server revenue, up from $74B

open.label: Backlog is not revenue
open.text: Dell does not say how much of the backlog ships this fiscal year or what customers can cancel. PC revenue grew 3% and its operating income fell 6%.

stories.headline: US blacklists Megaspeed and six linked firms, one an Alibaba unit, over chip diversion risk
stories.dek: Exports to the seven now need a license that will normally be denied. Megaspeed sits at the center of the reports around Jensen Huang.

facts.text: entities added to the Entity List by the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security: Megaspeed International plus six others
countries named: three of the six others are in Malaysia, two in Singapore and one in Thailand. Megaspeed is based in Singapore
the presumption for license requests for any item under US export rules, including Nvidia's top GPUs. Shipments already under way get 30 days
what Alibaba's Singapore unit Apex Enterprise Solutions prepaid Megaspeed and others to rent computing capacity, a person familiar told Reuters

open.label: Disputed
open.text: BIS cites a risk of diversion, not proven diversion. Alibaba calls Apex's listing erroneous, Megaspeed calls itself lawful, and Malaysia says one listed firm is not Malaysian.

chart.title: Entities added, by country named
chart.note: Per Al Jazeera. Malaysia disputes one listing.

stories.headline: FCC clears SpaceX to launch up to 1 million satellites for data centers in orbit
stories.dek: It is the first US approval of an orbital data center network. Analysts call the idea technically and economically unproven.

facts.text: satellites authorized for SpaceX's Starmind network, flying between 500 and 1,002 km up
the most computing power per satellite in SpaceX's description, 175 kW on average
when SpaceX plans to start launching them, COO Gwynne Shotwell told investors in October
the FCC's approval of debris plans for satellites above 600 km. SpaceX wants a waiver from the five-year deorbit rule

open.label: Deadlines unclear
open.text: Via Satellite reports milestones from 2033 to 2040, while TechCrunch says seven years for the first satellite and 14 for all of them. Amazon, Viasat and astronomers had asked the FCC to deny the plan.

annual recurring revenue of Falcon Guardian, which secures AI agents, in its first year, CEO George Kurtz said
Zscaler's rise on Monday, while CrowdStrike fell 8.92% on a day the Nasdaq rose 6.51%

open.label: Not closed
open.text: The deal needs regulatory approvals and a Zscaler shareholder vote. CrowdStrike's release gives no expected closing date or premium.
